source_text: Ta is discipulus spiritalis vere recipiens Spiritum Dei, qui ab initio in universis dispositionibus Dei adfuit hominibus, et futura annuntiavit et preesentia ostendit et preeterita enarrat, judicat quidem omnes, ipse autem a nemine judicatur. Nam judicat gentes, creature magis quam Oreatori servientes, et reprobabili mente universam suam operationem in vanum consumentes. Judicat autem etiam Judos, non percipientes verbum libertatis, neque volentes abire liberos, cum habeant preesentem liberatorem ; sed intempestive extra legem servire simulantes nihil indigenti Deo, et Christi adventum, quem propter salutem hominum fecit, non cognoseentes, neque intelligere volentes, quoniam duos adventus ejus omnes annuntiaverunt prophetee: unum quidem, in homo in plaga factus est, sciens ferre imbecillitatem, et in pullo asinee sedens, et reprobatus lapis ab eedificantibus, et sicut ovis ad victimam adductus, et per extensionem manuum dissolvens quidem Amalech; congregans autem dispersos filios a terminis terre in ovile Patris, et recommemoratus mortuorum suorum qui dormierant, et descendens ad eos, uti erueret eos®; secundum autem, in quo super nubes veniet, superducens diem que est sicut clibanus ardens, et percutiens terram verbo oris sui, et spiritu per labia sua interficiens impios, et ventilabrum in manu habens, et’ emundans aream suam, et triticum quidem in horreum comburens autem paleas igne inexstinguibili.
pass_a_gloss: The spiritual disciple truly receiving the Spirit of God, who from the beginning in all dispositions of God was present to men, and announced future things and showed present things and narrated past things, judges indeed all, but is judged by no one. For he judges the nations, creatures serving the Creator more, and with a reprobate mind consuming their whole operation in vain. And he judges also the Jews, not perceiving the word of liberty, and not willing to depart free, when they have a present liberator; but simulating to serve outside the law in a way that is unseasonable, needing nothing from God, and not recognizing the advent of Christ, which he made for the salvation of men, and not willing to understand, since all the prophets announced two advents of him: one indeed, in which he was made man and was struck, knowing how to bear weakness, and sitting on a foal of an ass, and a stone rejected by the builders, and led like a sheep to sacrifice, and dissolving Amalech by the extension of his hands; gathering however the dispersed sons from the ends of the earth into the fold of the Father, and remembering his own dead who had slept, and descending to them, so that he might rescue them; but the second, in which he will come upon the clouds, bringing a day that is like a burning furnace, and striking the earth with the word of his mouth, and killing the impious with the spirit through his lips, and having a winnowing fan in his hand, and purifying his floor, and gathering wheat into a barn, but burning chaff with inextinguishable fire.

choices.why: The subject of the sentence is the Jews, who are simulating to serve outside the law in a way that shows they think they need nothing from God.
The Latin word 'Oreatori' is a variant of 'Creatori', meaning Creator.

pass_b_english: The true spiritual disciple receives the Spirit of God. From the beginning the Spirit was present to humanity in every disposition of God; he announced future things, showed present things, and narrated past things. He judges all people, yet no one judges him. He judges the nations, who serve the creature more than the Creator and consume their entire effort in vain with a reprobate mind. He also judges the Jews. They do not perceive the word of liberty, and they refuse to go free even though they have a Liberator present. They pretend to serve outside the Law at the wrong time, as though they needed nothing from God. They do not recognize the advent of Christ, which he accomplished for the salvation of humanity, and they refuse to understand. All the prophets announced two advents of his. The first: he became man and was struck, knowing how to bear weakness; he sat on a foal of a donkey; he was the stone rejected by the builders; he was led like a sheep to slaughter; he overcame Amalek by the extension of his hands. He gathered the scattered children from the ends of the earth into the Father's fold; he remembered his own dead who had fallen asleep, and he descended to them so that he might rescue them. The second: he will come upon the clouds, bringing a day like a burning furnace; he will strike the earth with the word of his mouth and kill the impious with the breath of his lips; he will hold a winnowing fork in his hand, clear his threshing floor, gather the wheat into his barn, and burn the chaff with unquenchable fire.

review.notes: The translation accurately captures the Latin text. Pass A is a faithful clause-by-clause translation. Pass B is a fluent rendering that preserves all nuances, including the distinction between the two advents and the specific imagery of the prophets. The OCR error 'Oreatori' is correctly identified in the lemmas as 'Creatori'.
